note: Live-coaching policy status by game and mode. This is a maintained record, not legal advice. Every entry must be re-reviewed by a person before release and at least every reviewMaxAgeDays; stale entries are automatically treated as needs_publisher_review. Tournament and event rules are a separate, stricter layer (the in-app tournament switch disables all coaching output).

sources.title: Riot's Stance (VALORANT, third-party applications)
sources.excerpt: Unacceptable: applications that provide a measurable player advantage, such as exposing information that's intentionally obfuscated, taking actions on your behalf (botting or scripting), drawing conclusions for you during gameplay, and altering your field of intelligence. Riot wants players to review and analyze their games after playing rather than receive real-time analysis.

sources.title: Third Party Applications (League of Legends)
sources.excerpt: The same Riot list of unacceptable features (including drawing conclusions for you during gameplay) appears on Riot's support pages for League of Legends.

entries.rationale: Offline modes against the CPU (Kick-Off, House Rules, offline Tournaments, Manager and Player Career, the Practice Arena) with no other players, no ranked ladder and no Ultimate Team rewards. EA has not been asked; this is Sightline's internal judgement that live training tips here cannot disadvantage another player. It is not EA approval.
entries.reviewer: Sightline build (internal policy decision; requires product/legal sign-off)
entries.notes: Ultimate Team modes against the AI (Squad Battles, Single Player Draft, Moments, Live Events vs AI) stay post-match: they are online-connected, earn rewards, and Squad Battles is ranked on a weekly leaderboard. If the selected mode is wrong (e.g. actually online), the player bears the risk; the UI asks them to confirm the mode.

sources.title: How to play by the rules in EA SPORTS FC Mobile
sources.excerpt: EA lists bots, exploits, cheats and specialized software among prohibited conduct that gives an unfair advantage. No statement about screen-only coaching tools was found, and the console/PC user agreement text was not reviewed.

sources.title: Electronic Arts User Agreement (PC, 2022 version)
sources.excerpt: The 2022 PC User Agreement describes prohibited third-party programs as ones EA believes enable or facilitate cheating, modify the game interface or experience in unauthorised ways, or intercept or collect information from the game.

sources.title: How to play EA SPORTS FC by the rules (EA Help)
sources.excerpt: EA's FC rules page covers cheating, exploits and third-party coin buying; bans can cover all FC online play. It advises against third-party apps that can expose login details.

sources.title: EA SPORTS FC Pro 27 Official Rules (EA)
sources.excerpt: FC Pro 27 rules list using cheats, hacks or other third-party "helper" applications as a violation; an appointed human coach may be present.

sources.title: Introducing EA Javelin Anticheat (EA)
sources.excerpt: EA Javelin Anticheat runs on PC and shuts the game down when it detects software on its denylist.

entries.reviewer: Sightline build (automated web research; must be confirmed by a person)
entries.notes: Online, Ultimate Team (including Squad Battles, Drafts and Live Events against the AI, which earn rewards), Rush, Clubs, co-op and The Grounds: post-match review only until EA's position is documented. Division Rivals feeds FC Pro qualification, whose rules ban helper applications.

entries.rationale: Practice against bots on a local server, Workshop training maps and the player's own server with bots only: no other players are affected and nothing is ranked. This is Sightline's internal judgement, not Valve approval.
entries.reviewer: Sightline build (internal policy decision; requires product/legal sign-off)
entries.notes: If friends or strangers join the server, choose another mode. Sightline never injects into the game, reads its memory, automates input or draws over it; Game State Integration is Valve's own data feed and sends only the player's own state while playing.

sources.title: Steam Support: Valve Anti-Cheat (VAC) System
sources.excerpt: VAC bans accounts for cheats that modify or read the game; bans are permanent. CS2's Trusted Mode blocks third-party code from injecting into the game. No statement about screen-only coaching tools was found.

sources.title: Steam Subscriber Agreement
sources.excerpt: Valve may restrict or terminate accounts for cheating or for using unauthorised third-party software that interferes with games (summary, not quoted).

sources.title: Counter-Strike 2: 'Guns, Guides, and Games' (Mar 2026)
sources.excerpt: Valve added limited in-game map guides for the first rounds of each half in Competitive and Retakes and kept them off in Premier: light built-in guidance, which does not extend to third-party live coaching.

sources.title: CounterStrike2GSI issue #12 (library maintainer)
sources.excerpt: While playing, Game State Integration sends only the player's own state; positions and all-player data are available only while spectating.

entries.game: Any game without its own entry
entries.rationale: When the player declares an offline, single-player, non-competitive mode of a game with no registry entry, live training tips cannot disadvantage another player. Internal judgement, not publisher approval; a game-specific entry always takes precedence.
